Reading the Enemy Team: Pick and Build Against It

Spot what the enemy team wants to do, then choose a champion and items that shut it down: armor or magic resist, anti-heal, tank shredding, and answers to dive, poke and crowd control.

Look before you lock in

Every enemy team has a plan, whether they know it or not. Before you lock in (and every time you back to shop) ask four questions:

  1. What damage do they deal? Mostly physical (AD), mostly magic (AP), or a mix?
  2. How do they start fights? Hard engage, poke from range, assassins who jump on one target?
  3. How tanky are they? Count the tanks and bruisers.
  4. Who heals? Healing supports, life-steal bruisers and drain tanks all need anti-heal.

The answers decide what you should pick if you're picking late, and what you should build no matter when you picked.

Heavy AD or heavy AP

When most of the enemy damage is one type, defensive stats against it become extremely efficient.

Enemy teamPick ideasBuild ideas
4-5 AD championsChampions with armor or self-protection; AP damage so they can't stack armor against you tooPlated Steelcaps, Frozen Heart, Randuin's Omen, Zhonya's Hourglass (mages), Death's Dance (AD)
4-5 AP championsChampions with magic resist or shields; AD damage to diversifyMercury's Treads, Force of Nature, Kaenic Rookern, Banshee's Veil (mages), Maw of Malmortius, Wit's End (AD)
Pro tipBoots are your cheapest answer. Plated Steelcaps against a team of AD auto-attackers, or Mercury's Treads against magic damage and crowd control, can change a whole lane.

Tanks and assassins

Against tanks, pick and build damage that scales with their health. Vayne's Silver Bolts deal a percentage of max health as true damage, Liandry's Torment burns high-health targets, and armor or magic penetration (Lord Dominik's Regards, Black Cleaver, Void Staff) stops them from out-scaling your damage. Avoid all-burst picks if the enemy has three or four tanks: your combo won't kill anyone.

Against assassins like Zed, Talon or Katarina, pick crowd control and self-protection. Malzahar's passive blocks burst and his ultimate suppresses a diving assassin, Lux has a bind and a shield, Annie has an instant stun and Veigar's cage stops dives. Then build to survive the burst: Zhonya's Hourglass and Banshee's Veil for mages, Guardian Angel or Immortal Shieldbow for marksmen.

Poke, dive and healing

Poke teams (think Xerath, Jayce, Ziggs) want to chip you down before fights. Answer them with hard engage that forces a fight (Malphite, Leona) or with champions that heal and sustain. Never stand in a long line under their tower waiting.

Dive teams (Jarvan IV, Diana, Leona) jump onto your backline. Pick mobility (Ezreal's Arcane Shift) and peel (Janna, Lulu), and keep your carries close to the frontline.

Healing teams (Soraka, Vladimir, Aatrox, Warwick, Dr. Mundo) need Grievous Wounds, an effect that cuts healing. Cheap components give it early: Executioner's Calling (AD), Oblivion Orb (AP) and Bramble Vest (tanks). Full items: Mortal Reminder, Chempunk Chainsword, Morellonomicon and Thornmail.

Common mistakeDon't wait until your fifth item to buy anti-heal against a healing lane. Buy the cheap component early when the healing is winning you the lane, then finish it later.

Crowd control, split pushers and hyper-carries

  • Lots of crowd control (Leona, Amumu, Morgana, Malzahar): Mercury's Treads for tenacity, and Mercurial Scimitar or Quicksilver Sash to cleanse a key stun or suppression. Marksmen can take Cleanse.
  • A split pusher (Fiora, Tryndamere, Jax): pick a mid with strong wave clear like Ziggs or Malzahar, so your team can hold side lanes, and force fights on the other side of the map. The Side Lanes & Split Pushing guide explains how.
  • Hyper-carries (Kayle, Kog'Maw, Kassadin): they're weak early and monstrous late. Pick early-game champions (Draven, Lee Sin), punish them in lane, and try to end before they scale.

A quick example

Say you're the last pick mid. The enemy has Malphite top, Amumu jungle, Katarina mid, Jinx bot and Leona support. Run the four questions:

  • Damage: mostly magic (Malphite, Amumu and Katarina), with Jinx as the only real physical threat.
  • Engage: huge. Malphite, Amumu and Leona all have area crowd control, and Katarina resets through teamfights.
  • Tankiness: two tanks and a tanky support.
  • Healing: none worth buying anti-heal for.

So you want a mid who survives being engaged on and punishes an assassin. Malzahar fits: his passive blocks the first hit of an engage, his ultimate stops Katarina, and Liandry's Torment in his build burns down tanks. On the build side, Mercury's Treads against all that magic damage and crowd control, and Zhonya's Hourglass or Banshee's Veil for the moment Malphite flies in.

Your pick vs your build

Your pick is decided once. Your build adapts every time you shop. If you blind picked and the enemy team turned out to be four AD assassins, you can't change champion, but you can buy armor and Zhonya's Hourglass.

Every back, take three seconds to press Tab and look at the enemy items. A fed assassin, a healer or a stacking tank tells you what to buy next. See Items and Gold: How to Shop for the basics of shopping.

Want to practice reading enemy teams? Try the Draft Practice tool.

Key takeaways

  • Check enemy damage type, engage style, tankiness and healing before you lock in and every time you shop.
  • Defense against one damage type is very efficient when the enemy team mostly deals that type.
  • Against tanks, use percent-health damage and penetration; against assassins, pick CC and build to survive burst.
  • Buy Grievous Wounds early against healing, starting with a cheap component.
  • Your pick is fixed, but your build should change every game.
